business_problem: Scaling database with MongoDB to support growth and meet peak seasonal demand is at the forefront of a retail revolution in Latin America: this fast-growing logistics business specializes in last-mile delivery, with a focus on efficient and environmentally friendly services.
solution_summary: Scaling database with MongoDB to support growth and meet peak seasonal demand is at the forefront of a retail revolution in Latin America: this fast-growing logistics business specializes in last-mile delivery, with a focus on efficient and environmentally friendly services. Supporting 300% demand increases with a simplified infrastructure for 99minutos 99minutos was looking for a microservices architecture that would enable the business to implement application changes quickly, and which would provide the flexibility to unify developments across varied, independently operated regions. Operating in Mexico, Colombia, Peru, and Chile, the company’s expanding customer base includes well-known retail and e-commerce businesses. 99minutos launched in 2014 and gained early success running PostgreSQL on AWS. However, exponential increases in demand placed its systems under strain.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the operational order, inventory, and logistics data behind 99minutos's platform.

data_flow: Operational data from legacy or distributed applications is consolidated in MongoDB Atlas, where flexible document models support microservices, APIs, and downstream user experiences without batch-heavy synchronization. Upstream and downstream integrations include AWS, Google Cloud, APIs.

metrics: Its core model offers fast deliveries nationwide, including same day deliveries, and its name derives from the business’s original commitment to deliver packages within 99 minutes in select urban areas.
architecture_clues: The solution uses a microservices-based architecture.
The deployment integrates with Google Cloud.
evidence_quotes: “When I joined in 2021 we were handling 2,000 packages a day,”
“Eight months later, that figure was up to 50,000, and a year after that it was 150,000. That’s 7,500% growth in less than 2 years.”
“We needed powerful services that could scale at the rate that we were scaling, as well as building out our customer offering.”
